idea: A placement function should move only a subset of keys when membership changes. Virtual nodes smooth a ring; weighted rendezvous scores each server independently.
steps: Place weighted virtual nodes on a stable hash ring.
Assign each key clockwise and independently with a weighted rendezvous race.
Add one server and compare old/new owners and distinct replica preferences.
example: With one original server, adding a second moves only keys now owned by the newcomer.
concepts: More tokens reduce but do not eliminate imbalance.
SHA-256 gives deterministic placement across Python processes.
Unchanged servers retain their pairwise rendezvous order.
question: Does a three-times weight guarantee three-times these sample keys?
answer: No. Weight describes expected distribution over many keys; small samples can be uneven.
challenge: Change virtual nodes from one to 32 while keeping the exact same keys.
cost: Ring lookup O(log tokens); rendezvous O(servers) per key; replica enumeration can scan tokens.
